title: How to Start a Pay Per Call Business or Network
h1: How to start a pay per call business or network, step by step
description: Want to start your own pay per call business or network? Follow 8 steps to sign buyers, route calls, track sources and pay affiliates before going live.
faq: What do I need to start a pay per call network?

At least one buyer with an agreed price and rules, publishers or affiliates who can send matching calls, call tracking and routing software that ties each call to its source, and a clear payout process for affiliates.
How do pay per call networks make money?
A network is paid by buyers for each qualified call and pays affiliates a smaller amount for sending it. The difference between the buyer payout and the affiliate payout is the network's margin.
Should a new pay per call network use waterfall routing or real-time bidding?

A waterfall suits fixed agreements where buyers are tried in a set order. Real-time bidding suits calls that several buyers want, since each call goes to the highest bid. Many networks start with a waterfall and add bidding as they sign more buyers.
body:
To start a pay per call network, you need four things in place before the first live call: at least one buyer who has agreed to a price and a set of rules, a group of publishers or affiliates who can send matching calls, a tracking and routing system that records every call against its source, and a payout process that everyone can check. Pick one vertical, sign one or two buyers, write their rules down, set up tracking numbers per traffic source, test the whole path, and only then open the door to more affiliates. The steps below walk through that order.

How to start a pay per call network, step by step

A network sits in the middle: buyers pay for qualified calls, and affiliates are paid for sending them. Your margin is the gap between the two, so every step is about keeping both sides confident that the numbers are right.

1. Choose one vertical to start

Running many verticals on day one spreads your attention and your buyer relationships thin. Pick one where you understand what a good caller sounds like, such as insurance, legal, home services or debt. Each has its own buyer expectations, call lengths and compliance questions. You can browse the industries hub for an overview of each.

2. Sign buyers before you recruit affiliates

Calls with nowhere to go are wasted traffic and angry affiliates. Agree with each buyer, in writing, on:

  • Payout per qualified call and the minimum call duration that makes a call billable
  • Hours they can answer, including time zone
  • Daily caps so you never send more calls than they can take
  • States or countries they accept
  • Duplicate rules, for example how long before a repeat caller counts again

These rules become your routing setup, so the clearer they are now, the fewer disputes later.

3. Decide how calls will be routed

With one buyer, routing is simple. With several, you have two main options. A waterfall tries buyers in a set order, skipping any that are closed, capped or outside the caller's state. Real-time bidding asks several buyers at once what a call is worth and sends it to the highest bid. If you want to understand the second option, read how real-time call bidding works.

4. Set up tracking for every traffic source

Give each affiliate, and ideally each campaign or ad source, its own tracking number. For web traffic, dynamic number insertion swaps the number shown on a landing page so each visitor's call can be tied back to where they came from. Without this, you cannot pay affiliates fairly or tell a buyer where a bad call came from.

5. Put quality controls in place early

Short calls, repeat callers and blocked numbers are where networks lose money and trust. Decide your rules for minimum duration and repeat callers before traffic starts, and plan to watch each source's quality from the first week, not after a buyer complains.

6. Agree on payout models with affiliates

Most networks pay affiliates a fixed amount per qualified call, set per affiliate and per campaign. Make the qualifying rules match what your buyer pays for, so you are never paying out for a call you were not paid for. Give affiliates a way to see their own calls and statements.

7. Check your compliance obligations

Calls can involve recording rules, do-not-call lists and telemarketing laws that vary by location and by how the caller was reached. This is not legal advice: check your obligations, and those of your affiliates' traffic methods, with your own counsel before going live.

8. Test, then launch small

Place test calls through every number and buyer path. Confirm the call reaches the buyer during open hours, is turned away correctly when closed or capped, and shows up in reports with the right source and payout. Then start with a few trusted affiliates and grow once the numbers reconcile.

How these steps work in Insight Dial

Insight Dial is built for publishers and networks running this exact setup:

  • Buyer rules: waterfall routing supports hours, daily caps, state rules, blocked numbers, repeat-caller blocks and a pre-transfer check. Campaigns can target by country and state. See call routing features.
  • Bidding: real-time bidding pings buyers in parallel, and the highest bid above your minimum wins in under a second, with a fall-back if nobody bids. See real-time bidding.
  • Tracking: call tracking with dynamic number insertion ties calls to their source.
  • Quality: sources are graded Good, Watch or Poor, and sources sending too many short calls can be paused automatically. See quality controls.
  • Payouts: per-affiliate payout rates, affiliate and buyer portals, and downloadable statements. See payouts.
  • Compliance tools: spoken recording notices where recording rules need one, and do-not-call list handling.
  • Your brand: white-label portals let affiliates and buyers see your network's name.
  • Launch: a guided setup checklist and a test-call tool help you check every path before live traffic. Alerts can go to Slack, Discord, Teams or WhatsApp.

Pricing is pay as you go: a per-minute call rate plus a monthly price per tracking number, paid from a topped-up balance. Quotes are available on request on the pricing page.

Common mistakes when starting a network

  • Recruiting affiliates before any buyer has agreed to rules and a price
  • Sharing one tracking number across several sources, which makes payouts and disputes guesswork
  • Paying affiliates on a different qualifying rule than the buyer pays you on
  • Skipping test calls and finding routing gaps with live callers
  • Treating compliance as an afterthought instead of checking it before launch
